question.problem:
Consider the set $D,$ defined as

$$
D=\{n-{n}^{2}:n\in \{1,2,3,4\}\}.
$$

What is the infimum of $D?$

$inf(D)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The infimum of a set $D$ is the greatest lower bound of $D.$

If $D$ is a finite set, the infimum of $D$ equals its minimum.

First, let's write down all the terms of our set by substituting $n=1,2,3,4$ into the expression for the elements of $D:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1-{1}^{2} & =0 \\ 2-{2}^{2} & =-2 \\ 3-{3}^{2} & =-6 \\ 4-{4}^{2} & =-12\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
D=\{0,\,-2,\,-6,\,-12\}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}inf(D) & =min\{0,\,-2,\,-6,\,-12\}=-12.\end{aligned}
$$
